definitions.definition: A number in Einstein's equations that describes the energy density of empty space, which affects how fast the universe expands.
definitions.example: Think of it like a dial that controls how much the universe stretches every second.

definitions.definition: A fundamental number that determines how strongly particles like electrons interact with light.
definitions.example: It's like the strength setting for the glue that holds atoms together.

definitions.definition: A mathematical proof that any system of rules strong enough to do basic arithmetic cannot prove its own consistency using only its own rules.
definitions.example: Imagine a rulebook that can't check itself for contradictions without looking outside the book.

definitions.definition: A proof that no system can define its own truth within itself.
definitions.example: A dictionary can't define every word using only words from that same dictionary.

definitions.definition: A proof that no computer program can always predict whether another program will run forever or stop.
definitions.example: You can't write a perfect 'will it crash?' checker for all programs.

definitions.definition: A law stating that in any closed system, disorder (entropy) always increases over time.
definitions.example: Your room gets messier on its own; you have to work to clean it.

definitions.definition: A principle that erasing information always produces a tiny amount of heat.
definitions.example: Every time you delete a file, your computer gets a little warmer.

definitions.definition: A system that does not exchange matter or energy with anything outside itself.
definitions.example: A sealed, insulated box with no openings.

definitions.definition: The quality of being logically consistent, orderly, and fitting together well.
definitions.example: A well-told story where all the details match up.

definitions.definition: Something that must exist and cannot not exist; its opposite is impossible.
definitions.example: A triangle must have three sides; that's necessary. A unicorn is not necessary.

definitions.definition: Something that exists because of itself, not because something else made it.
definitions.example: A machine that builds itself would be self-existent.

definitions.definition: An endless chain of causes where each cause is caused by something earlier, with no starting point.
definitions.example: If every book is copied from an earlier book, you never find the first author.

definitions.definition: Existing outside of time, with no beginning and no end.
definitions.example: A number like 2 exists forever; it wasn't created and can't be destroyed.

definitions.definition: The ultimate foundation or source that makes everything else exist.
definitions.example: Like the soil that supports all plants in a forest.

definitions.definition: Traditional qualities assigned to God in Western theology: all-powerful, all-knowing, perfectly good, eternal, etc.
definitions.example: In many religions, God is described as loving, just, and unchanging.

definitions.definition: A set of symbols and rules for manipulating them, like a language with strict grammar.
definitions.example: Chess is a formal system: pieces, moves, and rules.

definitions.definition: A basic assumption that is accepted without proof, used as a starting point for reasoning.
definitions.example: In geometry, 'a straight line is the shortest distance between two points' is an axiom.

definitions.definition: A statement that has been proven to be true using logic and axioms.
definitions.example: The Pythagorean theorem is a proven rule about right triangles.

definitions.definition: Trust or confidence in something, especially when complete proof is not available.
definitions.example: Believing a friend will keep a promise even though you can't prove it.

definitions.definition: A verse from the Christian Bible: 'For we walk by faith, not by sight.'
definitions.example: It means living based on trust, not just what you can see.
